items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Walking after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen in walks of 10 to 19 minutes. You walked after 1 of your scored meals, but you need to do it more often to see how it affects you.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try not to eat dinner too late, as sugar tends to rise more after late dinners, with an average increase of about 9.2 mg/dL. You didn't have any scored dinners that started at 8 pm or later, so keep up the good habit.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You averaged 13.1 hours of overnight fasting, which is a good habit to keep up. In a study, adding overnight fasting to coaching changed some blood test results by -0.03 points, but more research is needed to understand this better.
